To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Epidemic Routing provides eventual message delivery with low latency and reasonable resource consumption in the presence of network partitions.

i) Epidemic Routing is a viable technique for routing in a network that is not connected at the time of message origination, ii) Epidemic Routing has the potential to deliver messages with high delivery rate and low latency in the presence of a network partition, iii) the performance of Epidemic Routing is robust to the presence of malicious nodes, and iv) Epidemic Routing can be implemented in a distributed fashion.
Epidemic Routing is an effective technique for message delivery in ad hoc networks with a high probability of partitioning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing routing protocols that are robust to network partitioning and can be applied in the presence of short range wireless links.
developing a routing protocol that allows for the delivery of messages in a network that is not connected, or that becomes disconnected during message delivery.
the design of routing techniques that can be deployed in the presence of network partitions, which is a common occurrence for mobile networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Epidemic Routing provides an effective means of delivering messages in a network where a path from source to sink may not exist.
Epidemic Routing is the best choice in terms of message delivery rate, message latency, and total resource consumption.
Epidemic Routing is an effective technique to deliver messages to destinations in partially connected ad hoc networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
epidemic routing is a viable alternative for ad hoc networks that are not always fully connected, or that have a high probability of being partitioned.
Epidemic Routing is a simple, robust, and effective routing technique for partially connected ad hoc networks.
Epidemic Routing can be used as a reliable and resource efficient method to deliver messages in partially connected ad hoc networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Epidemic Routing is a viable solution for delivering messages in the case of a disconnected network.
, in some scenarios, it is possible for a network of mobile hosts to deliver messages without any underlying assumption about network connectivity.
Epidemic Routing can be used to deliver messages when there is never a direct path from source to sink or in the case of network partition.
